signals.name: Funding round
signals.look_for: A company raises money. Note the stage, the amount and the investors, including corporate venture arms and sovereign or pension funds. Significant: a disclosed amount, or a named top-tier, corporate or sovereign investor.

signals.name: New fund or investment theme
signals.look_for: An investor launches a fund, or publishes a thesis, aimed at an area of technology.

signals.name: Acquisition or merger
signals.look_for: A company buys or merges with another. Note who, whom, the price if given, and why.

signals.name: IPO or listing
signals.look_for: A technology company lists publicly, or files to.

signals.name: Shutdown or failed raise
signals.look_for: A company closes, cuts back sharply, cancels a product or project, or fails to raise money.

signals.name: Government programme or grant
signals.look_for: Public money for an area or a project: a national mission, a research programme, a grant or an award. Note the funder and the amount.

signals.name: Regulation or mandate
signals.look_for: A law, rule, required standard, deadline or ban that forces or blocks adoption.

signals.name: Security advisory
signals.look_for: An official warning, directive or vulnerability notice from a security agency (for example CISA, ENISA or CERT-In) that affects a technology.

signals.name: Major outage or cable cut
signals.look_for: A major outage at a cloud, network, CDN, security or communications provider, or a subsea or terrestrial cable cut. Note who, where, for how long, the cause and the impact.

signals.name: Public tender
signals.look_for: A government or public body buying a technology, or inviting bids for it.

signals.name: Patent filing or grant
signals.look_for: A patent filed or granted in a relevant area, especially by a competitor, a big technology company or a surprising new player, or filed in many countries.

signals.name: Research breakthrough
signals.look_for: A measurable step forward: a new record, a beaten benchmark, a first demonstration or an independent replication. Incremental results don't count.

signals.name: Top-conference recognition
signals.look_for: A paper accepted at, or an award from, a leading venue such as NeurIPS, SIGCOMM, NSDI, USENIX Security, MobiCom or OFC.

signals.name: Prototype or field trial
signals.look_for: The technology working outside the lab: a demo, pilot or field trial, with the parties named.

signals.name: Spin-out
signals.look_for: A university or corporate lab spins out a company.

signals.name: Standard milestone
signals.look_for: A standards body starts a work item or working group, adopts a draft, or ratifies or publishes a specification (for example 3GPP, IETF, ETSI, ITU, ISO or NIST).

signals.name: Open-source milestone
signals.look_for: A project launches, joins a foundation, graduates (for example at CNCF or Apache), or reaches a 1.0 release.

signals.name: Alliance formed
signals.look_for: Companies form a consortium, alliance or industry group around a technology.

signals.name: Product launch
signals.look_for: A vendor or hyperscaler launches a product or makes it generally available. A preview counts only if customers can use it.

signals.name: Infrastructure build
signals.look_for: A new or upgraded subsea or terrestrial cable, cable landing station, network point of presence, data-centre or GPU region, or satellite constellation is announced, funded, completed or cancelled. Note who builds it, where, its capacity and when.

signals.name: Competitor move
signals.look_for: A company competing with Tata Communications launches, prices or invests in a technology, including in earnings calls or filings. For example: Orange Business, BT, Lumen, NTT, Colt or Verizon in networks; Zscaler, Palo Alto Networks or Cato Networks in security; Twilio, Sinch or Infobip in customer communications; Vodafone IoT, KORE or 1NCE in IoT; Akamai or LTN in media; Yotta, CtrlS or Jio in cloud in India.

signals.name: Named deployment
signals.look_for: A named customer runs the technology in production.

signals.name: Partnership
signals.look_for: Companies team up to build, integrate or sell a technology. Note it especially when it involves one of Tata Communications' own partners: Cisco, AWS, Microsoft, TCS, Versa, NVIDIA or Johnson Controls.

signals.name: Price change
signals.look_for: A price cut or a new pricing model, a sign the technology is becoming a commodity or being pushed to market.

signals.name: Market figure
signals.look_for: An analyst market size, forecast or survey figure, with its scope and date.

signals.name: Hiring surge or new team
signals.look_for: Many open roles for a skill at a named employer, a sharp rise in such roles, a new team or lab, or a notable hire or departure.

signals.name: Employment trend
signals.look_for: Official or reputable data showing that jobs or skills in a field are growing or shrinking.

signals.name: Developer adoption jump
signals.look_for: A sharp rise in downloads, stars, contributors or usage of a technology's tools.

signals.name: Single job ad
signals.look_for: A page that is just one job posting. A hiring surge is still caught as a signal.

signals.name: Event or webinar promotion
signals.look_for: Registration pages, agendas, speaker lists and webinar invitations with no new facts.

signals.name: Marketing echo
signals.look_for: A page restating an already-known product or announcement with nothing new.

signals.name: Opinion without news
signals.look_for: Commentary or thought leadership that reports no new facts.

signals.name: Routine update
signals.look_for: Patch notes, bug fixes and minor version releases.

signals.name: Award marketing
signals.look_for: Companies promoting awards, rankings or badges they received.

signals.name: Non-technology corporate news
signals.look_for: Culture, CSR, office openings, or executive appointments unrelated to technology.
